profile.name: Amiya_desi
profile.intro: I'm Amiya_desi, an independent developer focused on indie games; I mainly use Godot and also build websites, tools, and public project notes

columns.title: Creative practice
items: Indie game development: Godot, GDScript, C#, time mechanics, multi-window interaction, narrative, and puzzle prototypes
Websites and tools: personal sites, GeoScore, browser tools, public code, and content workflows
Self-hosting: Docker, VPS, Cloudflare, static sites, and blog content pipelines

items.text: WakeUpAtTheBorder: a Godot game mixing puzzles, dialogue, and combat, awarded second prize in the third GodotHub themed Jam track
DelayTrace: a Godot game about time delay, recorded actions, and replay, one of my more satisfying recent Jam results
TimeRewindLinker: a puzzle experiment with time rewind, replayed actions, and links to echoes of the past
Enhanced Save System: a modular Godot save plugin with GDScript and C# implementations
GeoScore: a public-web SEO / GEO audit tool
Mio's Window Wanderer: a multi-window narrative prototype I helped make

learning: n8n, AI-assisted development, and content pipelines

items.question: What is sayori.org
items.answer: It is the personal site of independent developer Amiya_desi, presenting Godot games, websites and tools, open-source projects, writing, and public links

items.question: What does the blog cover
items.answer: blog.sayori.org records Godot development, websites and self-hosting, AI workflows, tools and resources, project retrospectives, and creative learning

items.question: What is your current main goal
items.answer: My main goal is to complete and publish my first Steam game; other experiments, web tools, and articles will continue with real project and learning progress

items.question: How can I contact or learn more
items.answer: Use me@sayori.org, or continue to GitHub, the blog, itch.io, Bilibili, YouTube, and the guestbook
